newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia gold prices up on ringgit but margins bad.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia gold prices up on ringgit but margins bad.

text.p: Gold prices have risen slightly in Malaysia, partly due to a weaker ringgit against the U.S. dollar, but profit margins are still weak, dealers said on Wednesday.
"In my ten years' experience, I think this is one of the worst years for gold," a leading importer of precious metals in Kuala Lumpur told Reuters.
Dealers in Kuala Lumpur said 22K gold, the popular consumer choice, was currently retailing at an average of 245 ringgit a pound, compared to 236 ringgit on July 15.
"This used to be nearly 400 ringgit during the late 1980s," said the Kuala Lumpur importer. "It should at least be about 280 ringgit now, to call it viable."
Malaysia, a leading manufacturer of gold jewellery, uses more than 10 billion ringgit in value of the metal for both ornamental and industrial purposes in a year, trade sources said.
They said more than 345 tonnes of gold were imported annually while only about three tonnes were produced locally.
A global slump in gold prices has, however, taken away much of the lustre from the business, dealers said.
They said the trend was especially bad when the Reserve Bank of Australia announced in July that it had sold two-thirds of its gold reserves in favour of foreign currency backed securities.
"The ringgit has been a factor for the higher price in the last couple of weeks, but it's still not the main reason as we have to follow international prices," said another gold importer in Malaysia.
"In the Australian bank case, everyone feared there was too much gold in the market, so we all got hammered," he said.
Bullion in Australia has since rebounded to US$324 an ounce from 12-year lows of around $313 an ounce in July.
